Assam flood situation improves as water levels recede, 6.5 lakh still affected The flood situation in Assam improved on Sunday as water levels receded across most affected areas following a rain-free night, although more than 6.5 lakh people remained affected in six districts and the death toll from this year's floods rose to 66, officials said.

An official of the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) said floodwaters were steadily receding in several parts of Upper Assam, particularly in the districts of Charaideo, Sivasagar and Jorhat.

"We hope the situation would improve further during the day. This would help us provide relief in a better way," he added.

.MEA issues advisory for Indian Nationals on commercial vessels in Black Sea region The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has cautioned Indian nationals against taking up employment on commercial vessels operating in or transiting the Black Sea and adjoining maritime regions, citing heightened security risks amid the ongoing conflict.

In an advisory, the ministry said the security situation in the region remains "highly volatile", with commercial ships increasingly vulnerable to missile and drone attacks. It noted that attacks on commercial vessels have risen since April 2026, resulting in the deaths of five Indian nationals.

The MEA urged seafarers considering jobs in the region to carefully assess the risks, verify security arrangements, insurance coverage, emergency response protocols and employment terms before accepting any assignment. It also advised Indian nationals to remain in regular contact with their families, follow safety instructions and closely monitor advisories issued by Indian authorities..7 dead, 20 injured as rains lash Pakistan At least seven people, including two children, were killed and 20 others injured in rain-related incidents across Pakistan's Punjab province over the past 24 hours, according to the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), as reported by Dawn.

The heavy rainfall also damaged homes and claimed livestock, the report said.

Citing the PDMA, Dawn reported that 14 rain-related incidents had been recorded across the province as of 2 pm on Saturday. The incidents included fatalities caused by building collapses and drowning, injuries resulting from roof collapses and electrocution, the collapse of seven house roofs, and the death of five buffaloes..French authorities say 220,000 now evacuated from forest fires .23 missing after Vietnamese vessel sinks in South China Sea .Taiwan detects Chinese military activity around territory Taiwan's Ministry of National Defence (MND) said on Sunday that it had detected four sorties by Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) aircraft, seven People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) vessels and three official Chinese ships operating around the island as of 6 am (local time)..Assam Cabinet approves stamp duty waiver for SHG loans up to Rs 10 lakh The Assam government on Saturday approved the waiver of stamp duty on individual loan documents executed by Self-Help Group (SHG) members under the Assam State Rural Livelihoods Mission (ASRLM) for loans up to Rs 10 lakh.

The decision was taken during the state cabinet meeting held in Guwahati under the chairmanship of Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma.

Announcing the cabinet decisions, CM Sarma said, "The state cabinet has approved the waiver of stamp duty on individual loan documents executed by Self-Help Group (SHG) members under Assam State Rural Livelihoods Mission (ASRLM) for loans up to Rs 10 lakh obtained from Scheduled Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Cooperative Banks or other Financial Institutions regulated by the Reserve Bank of India for livelihood and enterprise purposes."

"The State Cabinet has approved the Assam Ayurvedic Health Services Rules, 2026. The Service Rules shall regulate the recruitment and the service conditions of the services of the Medical Officers (AYURVEDA) appointed to the Assam Ayurvedic Health Service under the Health and Family Welfare Department. The State Cabinet has approved the mode of procurement for Masur Dal and Sugar for the period from October 2026 to March 2027, with procurement to be undertaken through NAFED, which will float the tender and discover the rates for supply of Masur Dal and Sugar on the basis of open market rates," the Chief Minister said..Nepal seeks India's nod to recognise National Identity Card for cross-broder travel Nepal has asked India to recognise its biometric National Identity (NID) card as a valid travel document for cross-border movement, seeking to allow its use alongside passports and citizenship certificates.

According to The Kathmandu Post, the proposal has been sent to New Delhi through diplomatic channels, and Nepal's Department of Immigration (DoI) is awaiting India's response.

"We have already forwarded the proposal to the Indian side through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs," said Ram Chandra Tiwari, director general at the DoI, as reported by The Kathmandu Post.

If approved, the biometric NID card would become an additional officially recognised document for travel between Nepal and India, complementing the existing passport and citizenship certificate system..President Murmu arrives in Delhi after three-nation European tour President Droupadi Murmu returned to India after concluding a three-nation tour of Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania, aimed at strengthening India's ties with the three European countries.

During the visit, Murmu became the first Indian head of state to visit Moldova and North Macedonia, while her trip to Romania marked the first presidential visit from India in over three decades.

The tour saw agreements to deepen cooperation in sectors including agriculture, healthcare, renewable energy, defence, tourism and trade. India and Romania also agreed to work towards doubling bilateral trade over the next three years and discussed a Mobility Partnership Agreement for skilled professionals.

Murmu addressed business forums in North Macedonia and Romania, spoke at the North Macedonian Assembly, unveiled a bust of Mahatma Gandhi in Skopje, and received an honorary doctorate from the Bucharest University of Economic Studies in Romania..Typhoon Noul makes landfall in southern China, with over 340,000 evacuated and flights canceled Typhoon Noul made landfall in China's southern Guangdong province, bringing strong winds and heavy rain to the region, including Hong Kong, and prompting large-scale evacuations and travel disruptions.

The storm struck Huidong county near Huizhou at around 3:50 am local time, with maximum sustained winds of 145 kmph (90 mph). More than 340,000 people were evacuated in Guangdong ahead of the storm, while train services across the province were suspended.

In Hong Kong, over 150 flights were cancelled over the weekend, and parts of scaffolding on a high-rise building collapsed, though no injuries were reported. Heavy rain and strong winds also affected parts of Fujian province and southern and eastern Taiwan as Noul weakened while moving inland.

Authorities remained on high alert as adverse weather conditions continued across southern China..Magnitude 3.7 earthquake hits Nashik, Maharashtra A 3.7-magnitude earthquake struck Nashik, Maharashtra, at 11:55:50 pm IST on Friday, with its epicentre at 20.407Â°N, 73.676Â°E and a depth of 5 km, according to the National Center for Seismology.

Berlin is now considering buying the missiles which have a range of more than 500 kilometres. Germany is in the process of modernizing and expanding its military in response to what it sees as a growing threat from Russia. The missile test came just hours after Germany said it held Russia responsible for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport in August. "In terms of protecting Germany and our allies, this test marks a new chapter in deterrence and maritime defence readiness," navy chief Jan Christian Kaack said. The Lora missiles are designed for rapid deployment from ships at sea. Germany’s own Taurus missiles also have a range of more than 500 kilometres, but are launched from fighter jets. According to reports on Wednesday from Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper, and public broadcasters NDR and WDR, one suspect is an ethnic Russian holding a Latvian passport. The second is a man from Belarus that holds a Russian passport. On Tuesday, Germany said it believed that Russia was behind the attempted drone attack targeting a Ukrainian transport aircraft at the airport in early August. Berlin said there would be strong consequences for the hybrid attack and has announced the closure of Russian consulate in Bonn and of the Russian House in Berlin , a cultural center that Germany believes to be inolved in in spying activity. It is estimated to cost between €15.6 billion and €35.2 billion ($18.1 billion and $40.8 billion). Germany's plans to increase its electricity capacity by up to 11 gigawatts over five years required approval of the European Commission to ensure they do not distort competition within the bloc. Germany set a goal of having at least 80% of its electricity come from renewable sources by 2030. https://p.dw.com/p/5KRHS Skip next section Sabotage probe opened in second power station attack near Cologne 09/02/2026 September 2, 2026 Sabotage probe opened in second power station attack near Cologne North Rhine-Westphalia’s Interior Minister Herbert Reul on Wednesday said an incident at a power station in Bergheim near Cologne is preliminarily being investigated as an act of "anti-constitutional sabotage," using a German legal term applied for criminal acts aimed against the order of the state. On Tuesday night, police were called to the Amprion substation in Bergheim after bright flashes of light were reportedly visible. A short circuit affected several power lines, but officials said power supply to citizens was not affected. It was the second incident involving attempts at damaging electricity infrastructure in 24 hours. On Tuesday morning, power lines at a substation in the eastern state of Brandenburg hundreds of kilometers away were damaged by a projectile . Officials have yet to identify potential suspects involved in either incident. Police search for clues on Wednesday after a second power station incident Image: Thilo Schmuelgen/REUTERS Based on the investigation so far, Reul said the investigation is looking at whether the sabotage attack originated from abroad or had a far-left extremist motive. Last year in Berlin, a far-left extremist network known as the "Vulkangruppe" carried out multiple sabotage attacks on power grids and energy infrastructure in and around Berlin, leaving thousands without power for nearly a week in the middle of winter. "Now we need to investigate," Reul said. "This was intentional; it was a crime," Ruel said. "More sabotage, more hybrid attacks ... interference like this is not happening far away, it's happening right on our doorstep," Reul told a press conference. According to officials, on Tuesday morning, a projectile managed to carry a cable into the extra-high-voltage power line at a substation near the Jänschwalde coal-fired power plant, creating a conductive connection to the ground that caused a brief outage. On Wednesday, Brandenburg's state Interior Minister Jan Redmann said "we were damn lucky" that only one of more than a dozen "rocket-like objects equipped with a propellant charge" reached its target. He added the suspects had positioned the projectiles directly beneath the power lines near the Turnow-Preilack substation on the border with the state of Saxony. Police continued investigating around the Turnow-Preilack power station on Wednesday Image: Frank Hammerschmidt/dpa/picture alliance The search for suspects continues, and an investigation is looking into all possibilities. Brandenburg police said their investigation also includes disruption of public services, the causing of an explosion and the destruction of important equipment. "At this point, we must assume that the perpetrators had been on the scene for several days beforehand and had installed the necessary equipment," Redmann said. The construction and installation of the devices required a considerable amount of "technical expertise," he added. The train had been moving at around 200 km/h (125 mph) and the conductor immediately applied the emergency brakes. There were 238 passengers on board the train, which was heading from Munich to Dortmund. No injuries were reported after police searched the tracks and ruled out the possibility someone could have fallen through the door. The passengers were able to get off the train in the town of Lohr am Main. Germany's Federal Police interviewed the passengers there and took down personal information. The officers also checked to see if any luggage had fallen off the train. The rail line was reopened around 2:30 a.m. According to a railway spokeswoman, there was no technical malfunction with the train. German rail operator Deutsche Bahn declined to comment on whether someone on board the train might have opened the door intentionally. "Doors on the ICE don't just open while the train is moving," according to a brief statement given to Germany's DPA news agency. "The specific cause is being investigated by the authorities," it added. https://www.politico.eu/article/poland-d.text: A man has been arrested as part of an investigation by Polish authorities into a possible attempt to attack Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. Writing on X , interior ministry spokesperson Karolina Galecka said Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński and Special Services Minister Coordinator Tomasz Siemoniak had ordered measures to be taken following a “possible assassination attempt on the Prime Minister … as well as the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense.” Tusk later confirmed on social media that a man had been arrested in connection with the alleged plot. Advertisement Advertisement Officials from the police service, the government’s protection service and the Internal Security Agency held an emergency meeting Sunday at the agency’s counterterrorism center to discuss the situation. Following the meeting, Jacek Dobrzynski, Siemoniak’s spokesperson, told reporters that authorities are “treating this matter very seriously.” “Month after month, year after year, more and more threats and worrying messages are reaching the police ,” he said. “In this case, we are talking about a strong probability that these threats could have been acted upon.” No further details on the alleged plot were released and it remains unclear who might be behind it. Poland has been on the frontline of Russia’s hybrid war against Ukraine’s backers in Europe, and has suffered cyberattacks which have been attributed to Moscow. In recent weeks, Poland has also seen a wave of violent incidents in schools , including the death of a school caretaker in a knife attack. This story has been updated. Advertisement Advertisement
